Staurosporine is directly linked to the Macrophage colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor, which in turn is a target of Ent-Gloeosteretriol. This chain of targets ultimately leads to the 60S ribosomal protein L30e, putative. The integration of these pathways implies that staurosporine may act through a signaling cascade involving Ent-Gloeosteretriol, which could modulate ribosomal function. The presence of a putative target suggests that the mechanism may involve regulatory or structural interactions at the ribosomal level, potentially influencing protein synthesis. The evidence supports a role for staurosporine in modulating ribosomal activity through this indirect pathway, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
